subject: Service boundary, derivative clauses and feedback-license routing
messages:
From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
To: Susan Park <susan.park@edgepoint.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 22 Jan 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Service boundary, derivative clauses and feedback license — initial redline

Susan — attaching our MSA redline and a short callout of the items that matter most to EdgePoint and to us. Thanks for taking a look. Key points we want to confirm up-front: 

- Output ownership: EdgePoint requested "ownership of derived outputs" in your initial draft. We typically grant customers a broad right to use outputs for their business, but we do not assign ownership of model artifacts or claim exclusive title. Please confirm whether you mean exclusive assignment (we will need to escalate) or a commercial license for productization.

- Training / retrain: Our standard approach is opt-in training with compensatory terms or a technical isolation alternative (no training, but access to a model variant). Can you confirm EdgePoint's desired default?

- Feedback license: We request a limited, non-exclusive feedback license to use customer-reported prompts/feedback for quality improvements and safety; we can offer aggregation/anonymization carveouts. If you require revocable/limited feedback use, please mark the redline.

Attached: EdgePoint_MSA_redline_20260118.pdf (our annotations). If it helps, happy to run a 30-minute legal + sales sync next week — we aim to keep procurement moving but need to avoid language that would assign Redwood intellectual property outside of the normal license model.

Next steps requested from your side: 1) indicate whether the output ownership language is an assignment or license; 2) confirm training opt-in vs. mandatory; 3) flag any deal-critical timeline for procurement sign-off.

Best,
Marcus
Marcus Lin
Senior Director, Strategic Accounts
Redwood Inference
(Attachment: EdgePoint_MSA_redline_20260118.pdf)

From: Susan Park <susan.park@edgepoint.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
Cc: EdgePoint Legal <legal@edgepoint.com>
Date: Fri, 23 Jan 2026 10:45:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Service boundary, derivative clauses and feedback license — initial redline

Marcus — thanks for the redline and the clear questions. Quick responses and our position below (legal copied):

- Output ownership: EdgePoint intends to own the rights to outputs that are generated by our users and used in our product (we rely on this for downstream monetization). We are proposing assignment of those outputs (not model weights) back to EdgePoint so our product team can ship. If Redwood cannot accept an assignment, we will accept an exclusive perpetual license for productization. Either option is a deal point.

- Training: our preference is that Redwood not train on EdgePoint data without explicit written consent. We propose an opt-in model that requires an additional commercial term.

- Feedback license: we are open to a limited feedback license but need a guarantee that any feedback used for product improvements will be anonymized and that EdgePoint can opt out of feedback use for specific datasets.

Timeline: procurement needs signed MSA + order form by 5 Feb to hit our product launch. We've posted our counter-redline to the DocuSign link (see attached).

Regards,
Susan Park
Head of Platform Partnerships
EdgePoint
(Attachment: EdgePoint_counter_redline_20260123.pdf)

On Thu, Jan 22, 2026 at 09:12 AM Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com> wrote:
> Susan — attaching our MSA redline and a short callout of the items that matter most to EdgePoint and to us....

From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 24 Jan 2026 08:03:00 -0800
Subject: RE: Service boundary, derivative clauses and feedback license — internal counsel notes

Marcus / Ben — quick internal read from legal (attached is our playbook snippet):

- Do not accept assignment of outputs. Assignment language creates IP transfer risk we do not take for hosted inference services. Counter with: non-exclusive, perpetual, transferable (or sublicensable) license to use customer-generated outputs for their product, with explicit carveouts for model artifacts and training data.

- Training: agree to opt-in only. If EdgePoint insists on no training, offer an alternate: a customer-isolated model instance or a private deployment (Redwood Private) with pricing uplift.

- Feedback license: we can agree to a narrow feedback license restricted to aggregated, de-identified metrics and safety signals; revocable on a per-project basis. Propose language: "Redwood may use aggregated, de-identified Customer feedback for model improvement; Customer may opt out in writing for specific datasets."

Action items for Marcus:
1) Push back on assignment; offer the non-exclusive license + a productization fee or mutually agreed evidence (e.g., revenue share) if they insist on exclusivity.
2) Offer explicit opt-in path for training with pricing buckets and an enterprise-only private deployment option.
3) Prepare a proposed redline that incorporates the license language and opt-in training options (I can draft).

Laura Bennett
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference
(Attachment: legal-playbook-msaredline-snippet.pdf)

From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
To: Susan Park <susan.park@edgepoint.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 26 Jan 2026 16:45:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Service boundary, derivative clauses and feedback license — proposed compromise

Susan — thanks for the quick turn. We want to keep your launch timeline intact and propose this compromise so procurement can proceed: 

Proposed commercial compromise (high level):
- Outputs: Redwood will grant EdgePoint a worldwide, non-exclusive, perpetual, transferable license to use outputs produced by EdgePoint users for productization and monetization. Redwood retains ownership of model weights, training code, and derived model artifacts.
- Training / Retrain: Redwood will not train on EdgePoint data without explicit, documented opt-in. If EdgePoint requests training, we will provide a commercial proposal (pricing + time-window) or the option to run a private deployment (VPC/on-prem) with a higher fee.
- Feedback license: Redwood will have a limited, non-exclusive license to use aggregated and de-identified feedback and telemetry for model improvements and safety. EdgePoint can opt out of feedback use for specific datasets by providing written notice.

Attached is a short redline that implements these points: redline-proposal-20260126.docx. Also included is a DocuSign-ready order form link so procurement can sign the commercial terms quickly if the legal language above is acceptable. If EdgePoint needs exclusivity instead of the license above, we will need to surface that to product/legal to discuss revenue-share or a bespoke arrangement (this will add time).

Can you confirm acceptance of the license approach today or tomorrow? We can push a final MSA + OF to DocuSign immediately and loop in procurement.

Best,
Marcus Lin
Senior Director, Strategic Accounts
Redwood Inference
(Links: https://hubspot.redwood.example/deal/EP-2026-045, https://docusign.com/edgepoint/redline-EP-2026-045)
